text: Lemma. [minimal counterexample, \(p=3\)] Let \(Q\) be a \(3\)-group of least order with \(D_5(Q)\ne\gamma_5(Q)\). Then \(Q\) has class \(4\), \(Q''\ne1\) and \(d(Q)\ge3\); \(Z(Q)\) is cyclic and \(D_5(Q)=\Omega_1(Z(Q))=\langle z\rangle\) has order \(3\), with \(z\in Q''\cap M_5(Q)\); the last nontrivial term \(P_c(Q)\) of the lower exponent-\(3\) central series equals \(\langle z\rangle\), so \(Q\) is an immediate descendant of step size \(1\) of \(Q/\langle z\rangle\).

text: Lemma. Let \(p\) be odd and \(G\) a group with \(|\gamma_3(G)/\gamma_4(G)|=p\) and \(\gamma_2(G)/\gamma_3(G)\) generated by at most two elements. Then \([\gamma_2(G),\gamma_2(G)]\subseteq\gamma_5(G)\). In particular, \(G\) is metabelian if it has class \(\le4\).

text: The image of \([\gamma_2,\gamma_2]\) in \(\gamma_4/\gamma_5\) is spanned by the brackets \([L_2,L_2]\subseteq L_4\) of \(L=L(G)\), so it suffices to show \([L_2,L_2]=0\). If \(L_2\) is cyclic, the alternating bracket \(L_2\times L_2\to L_4\) vanishes. Otherwise \(pL_3=0\), hence \(pL_4=0\) (\(L_4=[L_3,L_1]\)), and dividing \(L\) by the ideal \(pL_1\oplus pL_2\oplus0\oplus H\oplus L_{\ge5}\), where \(H\subset L_4\) is a hyperplane missing a given nonzero bracket \([u,v]\), we get a graded \(\mathbb F_p\)-Lie algebra \(M=M_1\oplus\dots\oplus M_4\) generated by \(M_1\) with \(\dim M_2=2\), \(\dim M_3=\dim M_4=1\) and \([M_2,M_2]\ne0\). We show that this is impossible.

text: Write \([z,z']=\omega(z,z')w\) for \(z,z'\in M_2\), \(M_4=\langle w\rangle\), \(M_3=\langle t\rangle\), \([x,t]=\varphi(x)w\), \([x,z]=\beta(x,z)t\) and \([x,y]=\alpha(x,y)\) for \(x,y\in M_1\), \(z\in M_2\). A nonzero alternating form on a plane is nondegenerate, so \(\omega\) is; \(\varphi\ne0\) since \(M_4=[M_1,M_3]\). Pick \(e\) with \(\varphi(e)=1\) and let \(K=\ker\varphi\). The Jacobi identity for \(x,y\in M_1\), \(z\in M_2\) reads \[\omega(\alpha(x,y),z)=\varphi(x)\beta(y,z)-\varphi(y)\beta(x,z).\] For \(x,y\in K\) the right side vanishes, so \(\alpha(K,K)=0\) and \(M_2=\alpha(e,K)\); for \(x=e\), \(y=k\in K\) it gives \(\beta(k,z)=\omega(\alpha(e,k),z)\). The Jacobi identity for \(e,k_1,k_2\in K\), with \(u_i=\alpha(e,k_i)\) and \(\alpha(k_1,k_2)=0\), gives \(\beta(k_1,u_2)-\beta(k_2,u_1)=0\), i.e. \(2\,\omega(u_1,u_2)=0\). As \(p\ne2\) and the \(u_i\) run over \(M_2\), \(\omega=0\), a contradiction.

text: Proposition. Let \(p\) be odd and \(Q\) a \(p\)-group of class \(4\). • If \(|Q|\le p^7\), or \(|Q|=p^8\) and \(d(Q)\ge4\), then \(Q\) is metabelian. • If \(|Q|=p^9\) and \(Q''\ne1\), then \(d(Q)\in\{3,4\}\); for \(d(Q)=4\) the type is \((4,3,1,1)\) or \((4,2,2,1)\), and for \(p=3\) both occur (\(Q_0\times C_3\) with \(Q_0\) of order \(3^8\) as in Remark 6.4(2)).
